Britain’s liberal paper of record says Keir Starmer is about to fall on his sword. According to the Observer, the Labour prime minister is expected to announce his resignation on Monday and lay out an orderly exit plan after losing the confidence of his own party. 

The same machine that sold him as the adult in the room is now quietly drafting his goodbye speech.

Waiting in the wings: Andy Burnham, the “soft left” poster boy and “King of the North.” He backs a Palestinian state, attacks Hamas terror, and refuses to call the Gaza war a genocide — just enough moral theater to keep each camp half‑satisfied and fully confused. 

He’s already secured a parliamentary seat in a tailor‑made by‑election and is openly framed as the favorite to inherit both Labour and Downing Street once Starmer finally lets go.

Official London, of course, is still lying on schedule. Everyone knows the script: deny, deny, deny — then quit “for the good of the party” the moment the internal numbers say you’re already politically dead.

And while all this plays out, critics in Spain, Israel and beyond have been pointing out the pattern: whenever leaders at home are drowning in corruption cases, collapsing polls or internal rebellion, they rediscover Gaza, Israel and “international law” as a stage prop. 

Foreign policy becomes the world’s most expensive distraction technique — a way to shout about someone else’s crimes while the prosecutors, rebels and successors inside your own system sharpen the knives.

🔔 ZachXBT flags JuCoin reserves as users report withdrawal delays 

📌 Wu Blockchain reported that several users had raised withdrawal issues over the past week. ZachXBT also questioned JuCoin’s reported $511 million reserves, saying much of the value appeared tied to USDC and USDT issued on JuCoin’s own JuChain.

🌐 ZachXBT said multiple users reported problems withdrawing funds from JuCoin. The complaints arrived during a period of added concern around centralized exchange reserves and user access to funds. JuCoin attributed the delays to platform upgrades and restructuring, according to Wu Blockchain. The exchange’s explanation did not fully end concerns because users were also asking about reserve quality.

⚠️ “Multiple users have reported withdrawal issues on JuCoin over the past week,” Wu Blockchain said, citing ZachXBT’s comments. The issue remains developing. There has been no public proof that JuCoin is insolvent, but withdrawal delays often draw fast attention because users depend on exchanges to process funds on demand.
